title: 🏆 Sindarov Plays Game Of Tournament, Wins Final Event Before World Championship
summary: GM Javokhir Sindarov won the second edition of Clutch Chess: Champions Showdown 2026 with a final score of 20.5 points after three days. He earned $168,000 (including bonuses) and played the game of the tournament against GM Hikaru Nakamura along the way. GM Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu finished second, GM Fabiano Caruana third, and Nakamura fourth. The Uzbek star sends a powerful message to World Champion Gukesh Dommaraju in his last tournament before the 2026 FIDE Chess World Championship. Final Standings At the start of the day, Sindarov and Caruana trailed Praggnanandhaa by 2.5 points. But with each win growing increasingly valuable, that margin could be overcome in a single game on day three. Each win was worth 3 points and $3,000. Sindarov joked that he'd woken up on Thursday morning, checked his social media, and saw GM Yasser Seirawan and GM Maurice Ashley chose him as their commentators' pick. This gave him all the motivation he needed to win, he said, beaming. His victory required two factors: Sindarov played very well, but also Praggnanandhaa slowed down, especially in his last match against Caruana. In their head-to-head encounter in the first mini-match, Sindarov and Praggnanandhaa drew the first game, but the Uzbek star won the second. Praggnanandhaa sacrificed a piece for two central pawns but had to find the counterintuitive 21...Qc5, which regains the piece. In the game, 21...Qb8?? looked like it did the same thing, except that White had a tactical resource!

title: Istanbul To Host 2026 World Rapid & Blitz Championships
summary:
Istanbul, T&uuml;rkiye, will host the 2026 FIDE World Rapid &amp; Blitz Championships from December 26-30, FIDE announced on Thursday. GMs Magnus Carlsen, Aleksandra Goryachkina, and Bibisara Assaubayeva are the defending champions heading into th...

Istanbul, Türkiye, will host the 2026 FIDE World Rapid & Blitz Championships from December 26-30, FIDE announced on Thursday. GMs Magnus Carlsen, Aleksandra Goryachkina, and Bibisara Assaubayeva are the defending champions heading into the annual event that crowns up to four world champions. With less than two months until the championships, players and fans had been impatiently awaiting confirmation of the host city. Thursday’s announcement finally provided an answer, although the venue, tournament regulations, and registration details remain to be announced. 🇹🇷♟ Istanbul to host FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Championships 2026 Istanbul, Türkiye, will welcome the world’s elite chess players this December as the host city of the 2026 FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Championships, one of the most anticipated events on the international chess calendar. Freedom Holding Corp., FIDE’s strategic partner since 2023, has become the title sponsor of the event. As part of the 2026 cooperation agreement, Freedom supports not only major FIDE events like Candidates and World Championship match, but also chess training centres, school programmes, and talent scouting initiatives worldwide. FIDE President Timur Turlov (@TurlovforChess): “We are delighted to bring the FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Championships to Istanbul. Türkiye has repeatedly demonstrated its ability to organise world-class chess events while making an outstanding contribution to the growth of our game at every level. I would like to thank the Turkish Chess Federation and its partners for their commitment and cooperation. We look forward to celebrating the end of the chess year together in one of the world’s most dynamic and welcoming cities.” Read more: https://t.co/brNuikKStD The event moves to Istanbul after last year’s championships in Doha, Qatar, where Carlsen completed his fifth rapid and blitz double championship. The Norwegian won his sixth World Rapid title with 10.5/13, finishing a full point clear of the field, before defeating GM Nodirbek Abdusattorov 2.5–1.5 in the blitz final to secure his ninth title in that discipline. Goryachkina won her first Women’s World Rapid title after beating GM Zhu Jiner in a playoff. Assaubayeva won the Women’s World Blitz Championship for the third time, overcoming GM Anna Muzychuk 2.5–1.5 in the final. The event is once again backed by Freedom Holding, FIDE's main sponsor since 2023. The financial services group is led by FIDE President Timur Turlov, who was elected to head the federation in September. "We are delighted to bring the FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Championships to Istanbul," Turlov said in the announcement. "Türkiye has repeatedly demonstrated its ability to organise world-class chess events while making an outstanding contribution to the growth of our game at every level." Türkiye has regularly hosted major youth tournaments, such as the World U9–U17 Rapid & Blitz Championships in Antalya in December 2025. Now Istanbul is preparing to welcome the world’s elite, 14 years after staging the 2012 Chess Olympiad. These events would give the country’s leading young stars, GMs Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus and Ediz Gurel, an opportunity to challenge the world’s best on home soil. The regulations for the events are not yet announced, but last year's rapid championships were Swiss tournaments, while the blitz concluded with four-player knockouts after an initial Swiss stage.

title: Istanbul to host FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Championships 2026
summary: Istanbul, Türkiye, will welcome the world’s elite chess players this December as the host city of the 2026 FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Championships, one of the most anticipated events on the international chess calendar. Freedom Holding Corp., FIDE’s strategic partner since 2023, has become the title sponsor of the event. As part of the 2026 cooperation agreement, Freedom supports not only major FIDE events like Candidates and World Championship match, but also chess training centres, school programmes, and talent scouting initiatives worldwide. The championships, traditionally held during the final week of the year from 25 (arrivals)  to 30 December, will bring together hundreds of players from across the globe to compete for four world titles in the Open and Women’s Rapid and Blitz events. The return of a major FIDE world championship to Türkiye highlights the country’s longstanding commitment to the development of chess. Over the past two decades, Türkiye has established itself as one of the most active chess nations in the world, combining a strong tradition of event organisation with ambitious grassroots programmes. Through extensive cooperation between the Turkish Chess Federation and educational institutions, chess has become a familiar presence in schools across the country. Today, Türkiye boasts one of the strongest emerging generations in chess, with young stars such as Yağız Kaan Erdoğmuş or Ediz Gürel leading the way. In 2012, the city hosted the 40th Chess Olympiad, the biggest chess event in the calendar. Just recently, at the end of 2025, it successfully staged FIDE World Youth Blitz and Rapid Chess Championships. Beyond its chess credentials, Istanbul offers an ideal setting for a world championship. The city serves as one of the world’s leading transport hubs, connecting Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Americas through extensive flight networks. Its unique blend of history and modern infrastructure makes it a great meeting point for the global chess community. FIDE President Timur Turlov: “We are delighted to bring the FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Championships to Istanbul. Türkiye has repeatedly demonstrated its ability to organise world-class chess events while making an outstanding contribution to the growth of our game at every level. I would like to thank the Turkish Chess Federation and its partners for their commitment and cooperation. We look forward to celebrating the end of the chess year together in one of the world’s most dynamic and welcoming cities.” The FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Championships are among the most prestigious annual events in chess, regularly attracting top grandmasters and rising stars in a battle for some of the most coveted titles. The defending champions are world’s number one rated player Magnus Carlsen, who won both rapid and blitz titles in 2025, Aleksandra Goryachkina (rapid, women) and Bibisara Assaubayeva (blitz, women). Additional information, including the official venue, tournament regulations, and registration details, will be published shortly.

title: FIDE announces new appointments to the President’s Office
summary: The International Chess Federation (FIDE) announces the appointment of advisers and representatives of the President as part of the Federation’s new organisational structure, presented on 26 October 2026. The FIDE President’s Office, headed by Adil Kozhikhov, will focus on implementing the Federation’s strategic priorities and strengthening international cooperation. Its responsibilities will also include working with partners and national chess federations, as well as coordinating specific projects and initiatives. The following appointments will be made within the President’s Office, with each official responsible for specific areas of FIDE’s activities. Special Representatives of the President Emil Sutovsky – Chief Executive Adviser He will be responsible for managing relations with FIDE’s key strategic partners, developing major partnership initiatives and facilitating cooperation on projects of particular importance to the Federation. He will also carry out specific assignments from the President. Victor Bologan – Special Representative of the President for Global Development His main responsibilities will include promoting chess development and strengthening relations with national chess federations, including matters related to the FIDE Development Fund. He will also be involved in major digitalisation projects aimed at modernising FIDE’s operations and services. Particular attention will be given to supporting federations and implementing chess development initiatives in different regions of the world. Dana Reizniece – Special Representative of the President for Social Development She will oversee FIDE’s social development agenda, including the design and implementation of social projects in cooperation with national federations and partners. Her work will focus on expanding access to chess and supporting initiatives that use chess as a tool for social inclusion and community development. Representatives of the President Mohamed Al-Mudahka – Representative for International Relations He will contribute to strengthening FIDE’s international relations. Akaki Iashvili – Representative for Special Projects He will coordinate and implement special FIDE projects that require dedicated support and cooperation with members of the chess community. Willy Iclicki – Representative for Chess Participation He will focus on broadening participation in chess, with particular attention to amateur players, seniors and chess communities in Small Nations. Zhu Chen – Head of FIDE Shenzhen Office She will lead the FIDE Shenzhen Office and support the implementation of the Federation’s projects in the region. A new stage of FIDE’s development These appointments are part of the establishment of FIDE’s new management structure, designed to ensure a clearer distribution of responsibilities and more effective implementation of the Federation’s projects. The new model envisages an active role for the President’s representatives in advancing FIDE’s priority areas, drawing on their professional experience and international networks. FIDE believes that combining the experience of professionals who have worked in international chess for many years with new management approaches will help strengthen cooperation with national federations and partners around the world.

title: Sindarov takes Clutch Chess title ahead of World Championship match
summary:
Javokhir Sindarov won the Clutch Chess: Champions Showdown in Saint Louis after overturning a 2½-point deficit on the final day. The Uzbek grandmaster scored three wins and three draws on Thursday, including a brilliant tactical victory over Hikaru Nakamura from the black side of a King's Indian Defence. Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu finished second, 1½ points behind. The result gives Sindarov a tournament victory less than a month before his World Championship match against Gukesh Dommaraju in Geneva. | Photo: Lennart Ootes / Saint Louis Chess Club

"One of the best King's Indian games I've ever played in my life"

Javokhir Sindarov won the second edition of the Clutch Chess: Champions Showdown in Saint Louis, finishing the three-day rapid tournament with 20½ points. The Uzbek GM entered Thursday's final session tied for second place with Fabiano Caruana, 2½ points behind leader Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu, but overtook the Indian GM in the closing stages.

Sindarov earned $168,000 in prize money and bonuses, while also securing a tournament victory in his final competitive appearance before challenging Gukesh Dommaraju for the World Championship. The match will take place in Geneva, with the first game scheduled for 24 November. Having won the Candidates earlier this year, Sindarov has now added another victory against elite opposition before his first appearance in a world title match.

The Clutch Chess format gives increasing importance to decisive results as the competition progresses. On Thursday, each victory was worth 3 points, while draws counted for only 1 point, providing an incentive to play for wins. Sindarov made the most of the scoring system, collecting three wins and three draws to add 12 points to his tally. Praggnanandhaa and Caruana both scored 8 points on the final day, while Hikaru Nakamura, who had led after the opening session, managed only 4.

The final standings saw Sindarov finish on 20½ points, followed by Praggnanandhaa on 19, Caruana on 16½ and Nakamura on 12.

The contest for first place remained close throughout Thursday's six games. Sindarov began by drawing and then defeating Pragg in their first two-game mini-match, taking over the lead. The Indian grandmaster responded by scoring two victories over Nakamura, collecting six points from their encounters, while Sindarov obtained a win and a draw against Caruana.

In his first encounter against Pragg, Nakamura, playing white, had a clear advantage in the middlegame after 31.Ne5! (Black cannot play 31...Qxe5 due to 32.Ng6+, capturing the queen next with the rook from e1).

However, the US grandmaster was not accurate while playing with the initiative in the ensuing struggle, allowing Pragg to slowly restore the balance. By move 40, Black was already for choice in a position with all six major pieces still on the board.

With both major-piece trios well coordinated, it is the passer on the d-file what gives Black a clear edge in this setup. Nakamura soon erred in time trouble, and Pragg went on to get a very valuable 43-move victory.

Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu had very realistic chances of claiming the title in Saint Louis | Photo: Lennart Ootes

Consequently, Pragg entered the final two rounds with a 1½-point advantage over Sindarov. The two contenders still had to face Caruana and Nakamura, respectively, with a total of 6 points still available.

It was at this stage that Sindarov produced the most remarkable game of the tournament. Playing black against Nakamura, he launched a direct attack from a King's Indian Defence, beginning with a bishop sacrifice and subsequently giving up two exchanges. The encounter featured several tactical ideas, with the Uzbek grandmaster maintaining the initiative and converting his advantage into a full point.

Speaking to Maurice Ashley afterwards, Sindarov described the encounter as "one of the best King's Indian games I've ever played in my life". Referring to his decision to continue sacrificing material even after obtaining a winning position, he added: "If I started playing beautifully, let's finish playing beautifully".

Meanwhile, Pragg had obtained a lasting advantage against Caruana, playing with an extra pawn for much of their encounter. However, the five-time US champion defended accurately and managed to secure a draw in a game that lasted 100 moves.

The combination of results left Sindarov half a point ahead of Pragg going into the final round.

Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu playing white against Fabiano Caruana | Photo: Lennart Ootes

Pragg thus needed to defeat Caruana with the black pieces, as a draw would leave him relying on Nakamura beating Sindarov (the latter had the white pieces). From a Slav Defence, the Indian grandmaster established a Stonewall pawn structure and sought complications in an attempt to generate winning chances.

The position eventually became double-edged, but Pragg made a costly mistake in the late middlegame, allowing Caruana to trap his queen.

The American converted the resulting advantage, ending his tournament with a victory.

Sindarov, meanwhile, drew his final game against Nakamura, securing overall victory by a margin of 1½ points. The result comes at a useful moment for the 20-year-old Uzbek, who will now turn his attention to the World Championship match against Gukesh.
